class.name: AABBi
class.brief_description: A 3D axis-aligned bounding box using integer coordinates.
class.description: The [AABBi] built-in [Variant] type represents an axis-aligned bounding box in a 3D space, using integer coordinates. It is defined by its [member position] and [member size], which are [Vector3i]. It is frequently used for fast overlap tests (see [method intersects]). For floating-point coordinates, see [AABB]. The 2D equivalent to [AABBi] is [Rect2i]. [b]Note:[/b] Negative values for [member size] are not supported. With negative size, most [AABBi] methods do not work correctly. Use [method abs] to get an equivalent [AABBi] with a non-negative size. [b]Note:[/b] In a boolean context, an [AABBi] evaluates to [code]false[/code] if both [member position] and [member size] are zero (equal to [constant Vector3i.ZERO]). Otherwise, it always evaluates to [code]true[/code].

constructor.name: AABBi
constructor.description: Constructs an [AABBi] with its [member position] and [member size] set to [constant Vector3i.ZERO].

constructor.name: AABBi
constructor.description: Constructs an [AABBi] as a copy of the given [AABBi].

constructor.name: AABBi
constructor.description: Constructs an [AABBi] from an [AABB]. The floating-point coordinates are truncated.

constructor.name: AABBi
constructor.description: Constructs an [AABBi] by [param position] and [param size].

method.name: abs
method.description: Returns an [AABBi] equivalent to this bounding box, with its width, height, and depth modified to be non-negative values. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var box = AABBi(Vector3i(5, 0, 5), Vector3i(-20, -10, -5)) var absolute = box.abs() print(absolute.position) # Prints (-15, -10, 0) print(absolute.size) # Prints (20, 10, 5) [/gdscript] [csharp] var box = new AabbI(new Vector3I(5, 0, 5), new Vector3I(-20, -10, -5)); var absolute = box.Abs(); GD.Print(absolute.Position); // Prints (-15, -10, 0) GD.Print(absolute.Size); // Prints (20, 10, 5) [/csharp] [/codeblocks] [b]Note:[/b] It's recommended to use this method when [member size] is negative, as most other methods in Godot assume that the [member size]'s components are greater than [code]0[/code].

method.name: encloses
expand
method.description:
Returns a copy of this bounding box expanded to align the edges with the given [param to_point], if necessary. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var box = AABBi(Vector3i(0, 0, 0), Vector3i(5, 2, 5))
box = box.expand(Vector3i(10, 0, 0)) print(box.position) # Prints (0, 0, 0) print(box.size) # Prints (10, 2, 5)
box = box.expand(Vector3i(-5, 0, 5)) print(box.position) # Prints (-5, 0, 0) print(box.size) # Prints (15, 2, 5) [/gdscript] [csharp] var box = new AabbI(new Vector3I(0, 0, 0), new Vector3I(5, 2, 5));
box = box.Expand(new Vector3I(10, 0, 0)); GD.Print(box.Position); // Prints (0, 0, 0) GD.Print(box.Size); // Prints (10, 2, 5)
box = box.Expand(new Vector3I(-5, 0, 5)); GD.Print(box.Position); // Prints (-5, 0, 0) GD.Print(box.Size); // Prints (15, 2, 5) [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: get_center
method.description: Returns the center point of the bounding box.

method.name: get_endpoint
method.description: Returns the position of one of the 8 vertices that compose this bounding box. With an [param idx] of [code]0[/code] this is the same as [member position], and an [param idx] of [code]7[/code] is the same as [member end].

method.name: get_longest_axis
get_longest_axis_index
method.description: Returns the index to the longest axis of this bounding box's [member size] (see [constant Vector3i.AXIS_X], [constant Vector3i.AXIS_Y], and [constant Vector3i.AXIS_Z]). For an example, see [method get_longest_axis].

method.name: get_longest_axis_size
method.description: Returns the longest dimension of this bounding box's [member size]. For an example, see [method get_longest_axis].

method.name: get_shortest_axis
get_shortest_axis_index
method.description: Returns the index to the shortest axis of this bounding box's [member size] (see [constant Vector3i.AXIS_X], [constant Vector3i.AXIS_Y], and [constant Vector3i.AXIS_Z]). For an example, see [method get_shortest_axis].

method.name: get_shortest_axis_size
method.description: Returns the shortest dimension of this bounding box's [member size]. For an example, see [method get_shortest_axis].

method.name: get_support
method.description: Returns the vertex's position of this bounding box that's the farthest in the given direction. This point is commonly known as the support point in collision detection algorithms.

method.name: get_volume
method.description: Returns the bounding box's volume. This is equivalent to [code]size.x * size.y * size.z[/code]. See also [method has_volume].

method.name: grow
method.description:
Returns a copy of this bounding box extended on all sides by the given amount [param by]. A negative amount shrinks the box instead. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var a = AABBi(Vector3i(4, 4, 4), Vector3i(8, 8, 8)).grow(4) print(a.position) # Prints (0, 0, 0) print(a.size) # Prints (16, 16, 16)
var b = AABBi(Vector3i(0, 0, 0), Vector3i(8, 4, 2)).grow(2) print(b.position) # Prints (-2, -2, -2) print(b.size) # Prints (12, 8, 6) [/gdscript] [csharp] var a = new AabbI(new Vector3I(4, 4, 4), new Vector3I(8, 8, 8)).Grow(4); GD.Print(a.Position); // Prints (0, 0, 0) GD.Print(a.Size); // Prints (16, 16, 16)
var b = new AabbI(new Vector3I(0, 0, 0), new Vector3I(8, 4, 2)).Grow(2); GD.Print(b.Position); // Prints (-2, -2, -2) GD.Print(b.Size); // Prints (12, 8, 6) [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: has_point
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the bounding box contains the given [param point]. By convention, points exactly on the right, top, and back sides are [b]not[/b] included. [b]Note:[/b] This method is not reliable for [AABBi] with a [i]negative[/i] [member size]. Use [method abs] first to get a valid bounding box.

method.name: has_surface
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this bounding box has a surface or a length, that is, at least one component of [member size] is greater than [code]0[/code]. Otherwise, returns [code]false[/code].

method.name: has_volume
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this bounding box's width, height, and depth are all positive. See also [method get_volume].

method.name: intersection
intersects
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this bounding box overlaps with the box [param with]. The edges of both boxes are [i]always[/i] excluded.

method.name: merge
method.description: Returns an [AABBi] that encloses both this bounding box and [param with] around the edges. See also [method encloses].

members.member: The ending point. This is usually the corner on the top-right and back of the bounding box, and is equivalent to [code]position + size[/code]. Setting this point affects the [member size].
The origin point. This is usually the corner on the bottom-left and forward of the bounding box.

The bounding box's width, height, and depth starting from [member position]. Setting this value also affects the [member end] point. [b]Note:[/b] It's recommended setting the width, height, and depth to non-negative values. This is because most methods in Godot assume that the [member position] is the bottom-left-forward corner, and the [member end] is the top-right-back corner. To get an equivalent bounding box with non-negative size, use [method abs].

operator.name: operator !=
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the [member position] or [member size] of both bounding boxes are not equal.

operator.name: operator ==
operator.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if both [member position] and [member size] of the two bounding boxes are equal, respectively.
